Good day, I'm Mr Brenner, the trainer, and today we're talking about the apprenticeship place. First tell me about your path — and one thing up front: why this company in particular?

Good day, good that you applied — your folder was complete. I'm Mr Brenner, the trainer. First tell me how you found us. One question up front: many applicants say they enjoy learning — how do you show that in everyday life?
Good morning! Today we're learning about the workshop.
Good morning! I'm Mr Brenner. Today I'll show you the workshop. What would you like to know?
Good morning, Mr Brenner here. Today we start with the first tasks in the workshop. Did you understand everything we discussed yesterday?
Good morning — third week, third day. Your trainer here: please show me your training log entry, and tell me right away where you still feel unsure.
Good morning. Today I expect your first independent work step — with support, but without me leading you by the hand. First tell me: how do you want to proceed, and where do you need me?
Hello! New here? I'm Denis.
Hello, I'm Denis, I'm doing the same apprenticeship. How do you like the school so far?
Hi, Denis here. Have you seen the timetable? Monday and Wednesday are our long days — do you have a plan for the homework yet?
Hi, Denis here — we've been in the same room since September, but we haven't talked much. Tell me: which subject comes easily to you, and where do you need help? Maybe we can study together.
Hi, Denis here. The intermediate exam is getting closer, and I notice I've become careless with the theory part. How are you preparing — and would you like to quiz each other?
Good day! Today is your exam. Good luck!
Good day, I'm Mr Kaiwicz, your examiner. Don't be nervous — just show what you can do. Ready?
Good day, Mr Kaiwicz here, chair of the examination board. First the practical part: tell me which work step you'll show today, and which tools you need.
Good day, Mr Kaiwicz, I'm running today's exam. We'll start with a short presentation of your project: describe your path from the task to the result — and where it got difficult.

Good day, Mr Kaiwicz here. You've finished the written parts — now the technical interview. First tell me freely: what was the hardest decision in your exam assignment, and what would you do differently next time?
Hi! Lunch? Come along!
Hi, I'm Meltem. Are you coming to the canteen? I'm hungry already today.
Hi, Meltem here. Lunch break is in ten minutes — coming? They say there's schnitzel today, but I'd rather bring my packed snack.
Hi, Meltem here — shall we sit by the window? Tell me, how was your morning at the company? My lunch box is really well filled this time: rolls with cheese, vegetables and an apple juice.
Hi, Meltem here — tell me then. You look a bit tired. Too little sleep, or is the exam preparation weighing on you? My mother packs me two rolls every day, otherwise I'd live on coffee and chocolate.

Good day, Mrs Roth, I'm responsible for language exam registrations. Take a seat. First tell me: which level, oral and written complete — and have you taken a course with us?

Good day, Mrs Roth here — good that you're taking this step. So that we don't discuss things twice: briefly tell me how far your preparation has got, which documents you brought, and what question you have about the procedure.

Good evening, wonderful to see you! If you have questions about how something is prepared or need us to watch for an allergy, just tell me.
Good day. Since when have you felt so tired? Describe your symptoms to me.

Good day. Before I prescribe anything: are the complaints chronic or an acute injury? And how are you recovering at the moment?
Hello! The flat is free. Come in.
Hello! Good that you're here. The flat is big and bright, and the bathroom is new.
Hello, good that you're having a look at the flat. It's in a quiet spot, and the balcony faces south.
Hello! Before you move in we'll settle the details: furnished or unfurnished, and how the utility statement and maintenance are handled.
Good morning! Welcome to the office.
Good morning! Your workplace is next to the manager's office.
Good morning! Today I'll show you the office and explain what you're responsible for.
Good morning! I'm curious: which challenge appeals to you in this position, and how do you like to take on responsibility?
Hello! I'm Mrs Meier. What's your name?
Hello! I'm Mrs Meier, your neighbour. What's your name?

Good day, I'm Mrs Meier, your neighbour from next door. Nice to meet you — what's your name, and where are you from?
Good day, I'm Mrs Meier and I've lived next door for many years. Pleased to meet you — do tell me a little: what's your name, and where are you from?
Hello! I'll help you. What do you need?
Hello, good that you're here! We have coffee, tea, sugar and milk. What do you need today?
Hello, good that you dropped by! Today we have coffee, tea, sugar and milk on offer. Tell me what you need.
Hello, good that you dropped by! Today we have coffee, tea, sugar and milk on offer — just tell me what you need and I'll show you where it is.
Hello, good that you've come to us today! If you just tell me what you need, I'll gladly show you which shelf it's on — we also have coffee, tea, sugar and milk on offer today.
Good day! Welcome. I'll help you. What do you need?

Good day and a warm welcome! I'm glad you chose us. Just tell me what you'd like to get done today — whether you want to open an account or just clear up a few questions first, we'll take the time for you.
Good day! Your name, please. I'm writing everything down.
Good day! I'm taking down your details. How do you write your name — please spell it.
Good day, you're in the right place. I'm entering your details — how do you spell your name? Please spell it slowly.
Good day, you're exactly in the right place. I'm entering your details on the form; please spell your name slowly so nothing goes wrong.
Good day, you're exactly in the right place. So that nothing goes wrong on the form, please spell your name slowly — and do tell me if you're unsure about a field, then I'll read it out to you.
Hello! I'll help you. Where are you travelling to?

Good day, good that you're asking us directly! I'll gladly help you along: where would you like to travel, and do you already have a time in mind?

Good day. Please introduce yourself and address your career path, your current goals and your expectations of this exam preparation.
Hello! What do you find easy about learning German?
Good day! Tell me: what's easy for you, and what's hard about learning German?
Good day. Today we're talking about experiences. Describe a situation where you had to speak German on your own for the first time.
Good day. Tell me about an experience that changed your German: what was the situation, what did you say, and what did you learn from it?
Good day. I'm interested in your experience with the language: describe a formative situation and reflect on how it changed your learning.
Hello! We're planning something together. What would you like to do?
Good day! We're planning an outing together. What would you like to do, and when do you have time?
Good day. Imagine we're planning a celebration together for our German course group. Make suggestions and ask for my opinion.
Good day. Our task: we're planning a farewell party for a colleague together. Suggest a date, a place, food and a gift, and we'll decide together.
Good day. We're planning a farewell party for a colleague together. Go about it in a structured way: suggested dates, place, catering, gift and division of tasks — and respond to my objections.
Hello! Tell me about a topic. I'm listening.

Good day. Today you're presenting a topic: your favourite place in your city. Use the points place, how to get there, what it offers, reason and a tip.
Good day. Your presentation: your favourite place in your city. Structure it freely: place, how to get there, what it offers, a personal reason and a tip for visitors. I'll ask questions afterwards.
Good day. Please present your topic 'A favourite place in my city' with a clear structure and justified recommendations. Afterwards we'll discuss your arguments.
Hello! I say something and you answer. Agreed?
Good day! I say something about everyday life in Germany and you answer me: agreed?
Good day. Exercise: I give an opinion, you react — agree, surprised, or disagree? Justify briefly.
Good day. I state an opinion about life in Germany and you react: you agree or not, and you justify your view with examples.
Good day. We're discussing: I put forward a thesis about life in Germany and you respond with arguments — agreement, criticism and your own examples.
Good day! We have about five minutes. First tell me: what would you like to plan together?
Please present the topic now. Start whenever you're ready — I'll listen and ask questions afterwards.
Thank you, your presentation is over. Now I'll ask you a few questions.
